target_translation: No arena field. The IO callback's do_process builds the deserialized meta as an owned value (Box<ObSSTable> holding its Box<ObSSTableMeta>) and leaves it in the IO result, which the waiting caller takes: ObSSTable::bypass_load_meta moves the Box<ObSSTableMeta> into meta_; batch_cache_sstable_meta_ moves the owned ObSSTableMeta out of the IO result into the sstable (assign_meta) in place of its deep_copy into the tablet's arena, keeping the remain_size test on get_deep_copy_size() and its break; dec_macro_ref and inc_macro_ref read it through the handle. The allocator parameters that only fed the bypass read or received the copy go: the ObSafeArenaAllocator parameters of bypass_get_meta, batch_get_meta_and_bypass_cache and get_meta_and_bypass_cache, with the temporary arenas that fed them; ObSSTable::get_meta's ObSafeArenaAllocator * parameter, which becomes a bool bypass_cache (its test nullptr != allocator; true at dec_macro_ref's and inc_macro_ref's calls, false at every other call, since every call passes every argument); bypass_load_meta's ObArenaAllocator &, and the allocator parameter that set_upper_trans_version and backfill_commit_version take only to pass it on; and the ObArenaAllocator & of batch_cache_sstable_meta and batch_cache_sstable_meta_, which only received the deep copy. The test nullptr != arena_allocator_ in do_process becomes a bool the constructor sets. Owner: the receiver, the thread that waits on the IO handle, then the sstable that takes the meta; not counted. Rules: s3-memory.md 3.2 M6 (names this site: the IO callback returns an owned value), 3.3 H1; RULEBOOK 2.2 (ObSafeArenaAllocator row: one arena per task, results moved back as owned values, never Mutex<Bump>; a deep_copy into receiver memory is a move of an owned value; nothing that needs Drop goes into a bump; an allocator whose data the callee keeps goes), 2.3 (default arguments: every call passes every argument).

source_construct: allocator member of cross-thread class: common::ObIAllocator *
target_translation: No allocator field. The callback is a Box<dyn ObIOCallback> owned by the IO result (s3-memory.md 3.4 E5) and hands back owned values: a decompressed block goes into the KV cache by move (put_cache_block; 3.3 H5, charged by the KV cache store) or to the waiting reader through the IO result (read_block_and_copy's value, the sync callback's block_data) as an owned buffer. Only the multi-block path draws from the micro block cache's 4 GiB budget (s3-memory.md 3.7.2, owner 'micro block cache'): prefetch_multi_block's callback object and set_io_ctx's buffers, charged on the scan thread before the read is issued, and alloc_result's buffers, charged on the IO callback thread, each take a Charge on that Budget kept inside the callback (3.6.1 A2), -4013 at once on refusal. The single-block prefetch and both load_block paths allocate from caller-owned allocators today, so they become plain allocations and their -4013 branches are allocation-guards (3.7.1); read_block_and_copy's copy is one of them, since it runs only when use_block_cache_ is false and the multi-block path always sets it true. data_buffer_ is never set (alloc_data_buf has no caller) and goes. Owner: the IO result, then the reader or the KV cache; not counted.
